Task:
Research how major consumer/assistant products implement PERSONAL MEMORY, with citations (URLs). Deliverable: a dense markdown report (no fluff) covering:

1. OpenAI ChatGPT memory: 'saved memories' vs 'reference chat history', how memories are extracted/written, user controls (view/edit/delete, per-chat temporary chat), scoping to projects, incognito, what OpenAI documents about retrieval at inference time.
2. Anthropic Claude memory (2025+): memory tool, project-scoped memory, memory summaries, user-visible editing, how it differs from ChatGPT.
3. Google Gemini personal context / Personalization with search history.
4. Microsoft Copilot memory & personalization.
5. Cross-cutting: what data each stores, granularity (facts vs summaries vs raw), how conflicts/staleness are handled, privacy/consent affordances, opt-out defaults, enterprise/admin controls.

For each, state clearly what is DOCUMENTED vs INFERRED/reported by third parties. Include a comparison table and a short list of design lessons applicable to a product that wants to remember a university PROFESSOR's teaching/assessment preferences across exam-authoring sessions. Cite every claim with a URL. Do not write code.

**Atomic task treatment.** When the goal contains numbered steps or phases, treat them as sub-steps of ONE task and execute them all in this turn. Splitting them across turns is wrong unless they reveal an architectural blocker that requires the user's input. If the "steps" turn out to be genuinely independent tasks that should have been separate delegations, flag that in your final message and refuse the ones beyond scope.

**Root cause bias.** Prefer root-cause fixes over symptom fixes. A null check around `foo()` is a symptom fix; fixing whatever causes `foo()` to return unexpected values is the root fix. Trace at least two levels up before settling on an answer. In deep mode, you have permission (and the expectation) to do the deeper fix.

"> Update: Expanding to Pro and Max plans (Oct 23, 2025) ‍ Memory is now rolling out to Pro and Max plan users ‍ Whether you’re iterating on a strategy proposal, debugging an issue, or managing multiple projects, Claude picks up right where you left off. Like Team and Enterprise users, you get project-scoped memory (each project has its own separate memory), full control to view and edit what Claude remembers, and incognito chat for conversations that don’t save to memory. Before this rollout, we ran extensive safety testing across sensitive wellbeing-related topics and edge cases—including whether memory could reinforce harmful patterns in conversations, lead to over-accommodation, and enable attempts to bypass our safeguards. Through this testing, we identified areas where Claude’s responses needed refinement and made targeted adjustments to how memory functions. These iterations helped us build and improve the memory feature in a way that allows Claude to provide helpful and safe responses to users.To get started, enable memory in Settings. ‍ Today, we’re introduc
---
ing memory to the Claude app, where Claude remembers you and your team’s projects and preferences, eliminating the need to re-explain context and keeping complex work moving forward. Memory is fully optional , with granular user controls that help you manage what Claude remembers. We’re also introducing Incognito chats that don’t appear in your conversation history or save to memory. Memory is rolling out to Team and Enterprise plan users starting today. Enterprise admins can choose whether to disable memory for their organization at any time. Incognito chat is available to all Claude users. Memory built for work With memory, Claude focuses on learni
---
ng your professional context and work patterns to maximize productivity. It remembers your team’s processes, client needs, project details, and priorities. Sales teams keep client context across deals, product teams maintain specifications across sprints, and executives track initiatives without constantly rebuilding context. If you use projects, Claude creates a separate memory for each project . This ensures that your product launch planning stays separate from client work, and confidential discussions remain separate from general operations. These project boundaries help you and your teams manage complex, concurrent initiatives without mixing unrelated details, serving as a safety guardrail that keeps sensitive conversations contained. Claude uses a memory summary to capture all its memories in one place for you to view and edit. In your settings, you can see exactly what Claude remembe
---
rs from your conversations, and update the summary at any time by chatting with Claude. Based on what you tell Claude to focus on or to ignore, Claude will adjust the memories it references. Incognito chat Sometimes you need Claude’s help without using or adding to memory. Incognito chat gives you a clean slate for conversations that you don’t want to preserve in memory. It is perfect for sensitive brainstorming, confidential strategy discussions, or when you simply want a fresh conversation without context from previous chats. Your regular memory and conversation history remain untouched. If you’re using memory on a Team or Enterprise plan, your standard data retention settings apply. Starting with teams at work Memory introduces new safety considerations and we've designed the feat
---
ure to be useful in work settings, while avoiding sensitive conversations and topics. We're also taking a thoughtful phased approach to ensure these powerful capabilities are deployed responsibly, and will continue to evaluate and test how memory works across the different ways people use Claude before expanding availability. Getting started To see memory in action, enable the feature in Settings, and let Claude generate memory with your past chats at initial set-up. Ask Claude questions like “what were we working on last week?” to see what Claude remembers across your existing chats and connected tools. If you would like to bring your memory details over from a different AI tool or export your memory from Claude for backup or migration, you can follow these instructions . Memories could also contradict one another, such as “I’m training for a marathon” and “I sprained my ankle,” which made personalization less accurate. The new memory system updates memories automatically with ChatGPT keeping track of the details it determines are most important so it can continue building on the context you’ve already shared. If you prefer to revert to the legacy saved memories system, go to Settings > Memory >  and click the “saved memories” link below “Memory summary”. Will sensitive informatio

n appear in memory Sensitive information may appear in memory if you share it with ChatGPT. If you don’t want information from a chat to be used to personalize responses, you can turn off memory or use Temporary Chats. Temporary Chats do not use existing memories or create new memories. Why don’t I see anything in my memory summary You may not see a memory summary yet if your account is new, you recently enabled memory, or there isn’t enough chat history. As you use ChatGPT more, your memory summary should populate over time. You can refresh your memory summary any time Settings > Personalization > Memory Summary -> Manage then going to the triple dot menu and selecting “Refresh”. Does the memory summary include all my memories? Not necessarily. ChatGPT’s memory is based on a continually u

stom Instructions. For information shared via conversations, ChatGPT can remember relevant details for you. Legacy memory system How do I switch back to the legacy saved memories system? Go to Settings > Memory > Saved memories to revert to the legacy saved memories system. From saved memories, you can select “Try improved memory” to return to the updated memory experience.  How does “saved memories” work? Saved memories are details you’ve directly told ChatGPT to remember. You can add a new saved memory at any time – for example: “Remember that I am vegetarian when you recommend a recipe.” Saved memories work similarly to custom instructions, except our models update them automatically rather than requiring users to manage them manually. If you share information that might be useful for future conversations, ChatGPT may save those details as a memory without y
---
ou needing to ask. Like custom instructions, saved memories are part of the context ChatGPT uses to generate a response. Unless you delete them, saved memories are always considered in future responses. ChatGPT can manage saved memories on its own, updating, combining, or removing them when asked. You’re in control of ChatGPT’s saved memories. You can delete individual memories, clear all of them, or turn memory off completely in settings. To chat without using saved memory, use Temporary Chat. How do I enable or disable saved memories? To disable saved memories, turn off “Enable memory” in Settings >Memory How long does ChatGPT keep saved memories? The “notepad” of your saved memories are stored separately from your chat history. This means even if you delete a chat, any saved memories from it can still be used in future conversations.  We may retain a log of deleted Saved Memories for up to 30 days for safe
---
ty and debugging purposes. Saved memories can show up in past conversations. For example, if ChatGPT remembers that you live in San Francisco, it might say “Since you live in San Francisco…” when answering a weekend plan question. You can delete that memory anytime, but it won’t remove mentions from past chats. To clear that, you will need to delete the specific chat where it was shared. --- om-interblocks-callout callout-transparent"> Getting started with sharing You can share your personal project by using the Share button on the top right to bring up the sharing pane. Invite teammates in your workspace by individual email, group, or by using a workspace link. Invitees get two levels of access: edit or chat. Edit access allows members to update instructions, upload or remove files, and invite others (but not remove existing members) Chat access lets members see and interact with the project’s chats, files, and instructions (but not invite others) As the project owner , you can create chats, update instructions, add files, invite/remove members, set member permissions, modify the project name, and delete the project. You can only invite members within your workspace. Invite members by individual email, group, or by creating a shareable link applicable to your workspace. --- Inviting individuals or groups ChatGPT Free, Plus, Pro, and Go users can invite individuals by using the Only those setting in the sharing pane. ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu users can invite individuals or workspace groups. Type their name, email, or group in the text box. You can also set their access level at invite time (chat/edit). Once you click Invite, both you and the invitee will receive an automated email confirming the invitation. If you invite a group, all members of the group will receive an email invitation. In workspaces that use SCIM, workspace owners can control whether SCIM-managed groups are discoverable in the sharing pane for projects. content.text:
Memory FAQ
Learn more about managing memory in ChatGPT.
Updated: 11 days ago
How memory works
When enabled, memory helps ChatGPT automatically remember useful context from your chats, files, and connected apps to personalize your experience, so you don’t have to repeat yourself as often.
Memory controls are available in Settings > Personalization > Memory. You can choose to enable or disable memory at any time.
Memory summary
You can see the information that ChatGPT remembers in the memory summary. While the memory summary should capture the most important details, it will not include everything that ChatGPT remembers based on your chats. If you want to know if ChatGPT has remembered something, just ask in chat.
The memory summary is automatically updated with new context as you chat with ChatGPT. At the top of the memory summary it will indicate when it was last updated such as “2 hours ago”.
To make edits to the memory summary:
Type what you want changed into the text box at the bottom of the memory summary and it will update accordingly.
You can highlight any text in the memory summary to make a specific correction.
To fully delete something ChatGPT may know about you, you’ll need to delete every source where it appears, including past chats, archived chats, files, the memory summary, and disconnect any connected apps that may contain that information.
You can delete the memories shown on your memory summary page and turn memory off by selecting Delete and turn off memory from the three-dot menu. This does not delete your past chats. If you turn memory back on later, ChatGPT may create new memories from chats that remain in your chat history, including older chats. This control is available on the web and rolling out on mobile soon. 
Memories in sources
You can see what sources were used to personalize a response such as custom instructions, past chats, files, and memories by tapping the book icon below the response.
Tapping on a memory in sources will open an explanation on why that memory was used to personalize a response.
You can also make a correction by selecting the 3 dot menu (•••).
Sources are designed to make memory easier to understand and control, though they may not show every factor or source that shaped a response. Memory sources are not included in chats you share.
How we've improved upon the previous saved memories experience
The previous saved memories system often became stale and relied on users to manually manage updates. Memories could also contradict one another, such as “I’m training for a marathon” and “I sprained my ankle,” which made personalization less accurate.
The new memory system updates memories automatically with ChatGPT keeping track of the details it determines are most important so it can continue building on the context you’ve already shared. If you prefer to revert to the legacy saved memories system, go to Settings > Memory >  and click the “saved memories” link below “Memory summary”.
Will sensitive information appear in memory
Sensitive information may appear in memory if you share it with ChatGPT. If you don’t want information from a chat to be used to personalize responses, you can turn off memory or use Temporary Chats. Temporary Chats do not use existing memories or create new memories.
Why don’t I see anything in my memory summary
You may not see a memory summary yet if your account is new, you recently enabled memory, or there isn’t enough chat history. As you use ChatGPT more, your memory summary should populate over time. You can refresh your memory summary any time Settings > Personalization > Memory Summary -> Manage then going to the triple dot menu and selecting “Refresh”.
Does the memory summary include all my memories?
Not necessarily. ChatGPT’s memory is based on a continually updated synthesis of context from your past chats, which may be broader than what can be shown as individual items in a summary. The memory summary gives you a high-level view of that synthesis to help you review and manage what ChatGPT remembers.
Some details may not appear in the summary, including when ChatGPT determines they are less relevant or not appropriate to show in this view.
Is memory different from Custom Instructions?
Custom Instructions
 continue to allow you to provide ChatGPT with direct guidance on what you’d like it to know about you and how you’d like it to respond. For explicit information or instructions, you can add it to your Custom Instructions. For information shared via conversations, ChatGPT can remember relevant details for you.
Legacy memory system
How do I switch back to the legacy saved memories system?
Go to Settings > Memory > Saved memories to revert to the legacy saved memories system. From saved memories, you can select “Try improved memory” to return to the updated memory experience. 
How does “saved memories” work?
Saved memories are details you’ve directly told ChatGPT to remember. You can add a new saved memory at any time – for example: “Remember that I am vegetarian when you recommend a recipe.” Saved memories work similarly to custom instructions, except our models update them automatically rather than requiring users to manage them manually. If you share information that might be useful for future conversations, ChatGPT may save those details as a memory without you needing to ask. Like custom instructions, saved memories are part of the context ChatGPT uses to generate a response. Unless you delete them, saved memories are always considered in future responses.
ChatGPT can manage saved memories on its own, updating, combining, or removing them when asked. You’re in control of ChatGPT’s saved memories. You can delete individual memories, clear all of them, or turn memory off completely in settings. To chat without using saved memory, use Temporary Chat.
How do I enable or disable saved memories?
To disable saved memories, turn off “Enable memory” in Settings >Memory
How long does ChatGPT keep saved memories?
The “notepad” of your saved memories are stored separately from your chat history. This means even if you delete a chat, any saved memories from it can still be used in future conversations. 
We may retain a log of deleted Saved Memories for up to 30 days for safety and debugging purposes.
Saved memories can show up in past conversations. For example, if ChatGPT remembers that you live in San Francisco, it might say “Since you live in San Francisco…” when answering a weekend plan question. You can delete that memory anytime, but it won’t remove mentions from past chats. To clear that, you will need to delete the specific chat where it was shared.

How does “Reference saved memories” work?
Updated: 11 days ago
You can control Memory via two settings:
Reference saved memories:
 These are details you have explicitly asked ChatGPT to remember, like your name, favorite color, or dietary preferences.
Reference chat history
: ChatGPT can also use information from your past chats to make future conversations more helpful. For example, if you once said you like Thai food, it may take that into account the next time you ask “What should I have for lunch?” ChatGPT doesn’t remember every detail from past chats, so use saved memories for anything you want it to always keep in mind.
You can choose to turn on “Saved Memories,” both, or neither. The settings are flexible and you can change them anytime.
When “Reference chat history” is turned on, ChatGPT will reference your past conversations to recall useful information you’ve shared. It uses this to learn about your interests and preferences, helping make future chats more personalized and relevant. Like custom instructions, when this setting is on, relevant information from your past conversations may be added to new ones. Unlike saved memories, which are kept until you delete them, details from past chats can change over time as ChatGPT updates what’s more helpful to remember. Because ChatGPT doesn’t retain every detail from past chats, use saved memories for anything you want it to always remember.
How do I enable or disable Reference chat history?
You can turn Reference chat history on or off anytime by clicking your profile icon > 
Settings > Personalization
:
Turning saved memory off won’t delete anything that’s already been remembered. And deleting a chat doesn’t remove saved memory from that conversation. To delete saved memories, tell ChatGPT to delete or forget it, or go to “Manage memories” in Settings.
To fully remove something, delete both the saved memory in Settings and the chat where you originally shared it.

I read this as a research deliverable - I’ll distinguish first-party documentation from inference and third-party reporting, then compare the systems and extract professor-memory design lessons.

# Personal memory in major AI assistants

**Evidence scope:** Public product documentation and announcements available for the 2025+ memory generation. Some first-party pages are living documents and may describe newer behavior than the original launch. **DOCUMENTED** means stated by the vendor; **INFERRED** means an architectural conclusion not confirmed by the vendor; **THIRD-PARTY** means press reporting.

## Executive comparison

| Product | Persistent representation | How it is written | Retrieval at inference | Scope | User controls / private mode | Default / enterprise posture |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ChatGPT** | Two documented layers in the 2025 model: durable **saved memories** (facts/preferences) plus a changing synthesis of **chat history**. OpenAI’s newer documentation exposes an editable **memory summary** synthesized from chats, files and connected apps. Raw chats remain separate sources. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq), [saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work)) | Explicit “remember X,” automatic extraction of potentially useful details, and automatic updating/combining/removal; newer memory continuously updates a synthesis and attempts to resolve stale/contradictory details. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq)) | Saved memories are inserted into the context used to generate responses and, unless deleted, are “always considered”; with chat-history reference, relevant past-chat information may be added to a new conversation. OpenAI does **not** document the ranking/index/embedding algorithm. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq), [saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work)) | Account-wide by default; optional **project-only** boundary excludes saved memories and outside-project chats while allowing same-project conversations. Enterprise/Edu default-project chats are also contained within the project. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)) | View/edit/delete memory, ask what it remembers, delete and turn off; response-level source explanations in newer UI. **Temporary Chat** neither reads nor creates personalization memory, is absent from history and is retained up to 30 days for safety. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq), [Temporary Chat](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-faq)) | Personal toggles plus workspace memory controls; project and retention policies inherit workspace controls. Business/Enterprise/Edu content is not used for training by default. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt), [Enterprise privacy](https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/)) |
| **Claude app** | One user-visible **memory summary** derived from prior chats, with a separate summary for each project; raw conversation history remains separate. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) | On initial setup Claude generates memory from past chats; thereafter it updates the summary as work continues and responds to instructions about what to focus on or ignore. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) | Anthropic says Claude uses/references the summary and can answer across existing chats and connected tools, but does not document its consumer retrieval/ranking algorithm. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) | Strongly **project-scoped**: every project has separate memory, designed to prevent leakage between client/work streams. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) | Full summary visibility; edit by chatting with Claude; enable in Settings. **Incognito chat** does not appear in history or read/write memory and leaves regular memory/history unchanged. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) | Explicitly optional; launched to Team/Enterprise, then Pro/Max. Enterprise admins may disable it organization-wide. Standard Team/Enterprise retention still applies. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory)) |
| **Claude Platform memory tool** | Developer-controlled files under `/memories`; can be text/XML/images rather than a fixed fact schema. This is **not the same feature as Claude-app memory**. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)) | Claude requests `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete` and `rename`; the client application executes the operations. Claude checks memory before work and writes progress/preferences as it works. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)) | Just-in-time: Claude reads memory files on demand rather than loading all memory into every context window. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)) | Whatever tenant/user/project namespace the developer implements. | Entirely application-defined; storage, retention, visibility, consent and deletion are the developer’s responsibility. | Client-side/customer-controlled storage; Anthropic specifically assigns path traversal, expiry, file-size and sensitive-data safeguards to the implementer. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)) |
| **Gemini** | Three distinguishable sources: user-entered **saved info**, useful information from **past Gemini chats**, and raw activity from connected Google services—initially **Search history**. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/), [personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en)) | Saved info is explicit; past-chat personalization is model-derived; Search personalization analyzes prompts and conditionally consults the user’s existing Search history. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/)) | Google documents a relevance gate: Search history is used only when its reasoning model determines it is helpful. Responses can disclose whether saved info, past chats or Search history contributed. Internal retrieval mechanics are undisclosed. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/)) | Google-account-wide context, not a documented project memory boundary; source access can extend across Google apps, including planned/expanded Photos and YouTube connections. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/)) | Permission prompt before connecting Search history; source transparency; disconnect Search, manage Search history and saved info. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/), [personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en), [Privacy Hub](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en)) | Search-history connection is opt-in and also requires Web & App Activity. Availability and controls differ for personal versus work/school accounts. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/), [personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en)) |
| **Microsoft Copilot consumer** | Discrete remembered details/preferences plus a broader personalization profile; Microsoft describes remembering facts such as interests and using prior interactions to build a richer understanding. ([Microsoft launch announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/), [GeekWire launch report](https://www.geekwire.com/2025/microsoft-gives-copilot-its-own-memory-in-new-push-to-personalize-its-ai-assistant/)) | Users can explicitly tell Copilot to remember; product reporting says Copilot also detects useful details during conversations. Microsoft later added a user-editable memory/personalization profile. ([Microsoft launch announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/), [ZDNET report on editing](https://www.zdnet.com/article/you-can-now-edit-microsoft-copilots-memories-about-you-heres-how/)) | Microsoft says memories are used to tailor answers, suggestions and proactive assistance, but does not publicly document retrieval ranking or context assembly. ([Microsoft launch announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/)) | Consumer-account scope; Microsoft has not documented a ChatGPT/Claude-style project-memory boundary for consumer Copilot. | Ask what it knows; add, edit or delete memories; turn personalization/memory off in settings. Details of rollout/default state have varied by account and region. ([ZDNET report on editing](https://www.zdnet.com/article/you-can-now-edit-microsoft-copilots-memories-about-you-heres-how/), [The Verge launch report](https://www.theverge.com/news/643225/microsoft-copilot-ai-features-memory-actions-vision)) | Primarily a consumer feature tied to personal Microsoft accounts. It should not be conflated with Microsoft 365 Copilot’s Graph-grounded work context, which is governed through tenant permissions, compliance and admin policy rather than consumer memory. ([Microsoft 365 privacy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy), [Microsoft launch announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/)) |

---

## 1. OpenAI ChatGPT

### Saved memories versus reference chat history

**DOCUMENTED — 2025 two-layer model**

- **Reference saved memories** are durable facts the user explicitly asked ChatGPT to retain—name, favorite color, dietary requirements—or that ChatGPT judged useful enough to save automatically. They are stored separately from chat history and remain until deleted. ([Saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work), [Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- **Reference chat history** lets ChatGPT derive useful interests and preferences from previous conversations without representing every detail as a permanent saved-memory item. These details can change as ChatGPT revises what is useful; OpenAI explicitly advises saved memory for information that must always remain top-of-mind. ([Saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work))
- A deleted chat does not by itself delete a saved memory extracted from it. Full erasure requires deleting both the memory and the source chat; newer memory may additionally require removing files, archived chats and connected-app sources. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

**DOCUMENTED — newer evolution**

OpenAI’s current FAQ describes an “improved memory” as a continually updated synthesis from chats, files and connected apps, exposed through an editable **memory summary**. The summary is explicitly incomplete: it is a high-level view and may omit less relevant details even though they can still influence personalization. Users may revert to the legacy saved-memory system. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

### Extraction, writing and stale/conflicting information

**DOCUMENTED**

- Explicit write: “Remember that I am vegetarian…” creates a saved memory. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- Implicit write: ChatGPT may save information it predicts will be useful without a direct request. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- The model may update, combine or remove saved memories when asked. Newer memory updates automatically and was introduced partly because legacy memories became stale or contradictory—for example, “training for a marathon” versus “sprained my ankle.” ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- OpenAI says it has trained ChatGPT not to proactively remember sensitive information such as health details unless explicitly requested, but also warns that sensitive information can appear if users share it; therefore this is a model-behavior mitigation, not a hard storage prohibition. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

**INFERRED**

- Extraction is model-mediated semantic synthesis rather than deterministic field extraction. OpenAI does not publish schemas, confidence thresholds, deduplication algorithms or conflict-resolution precedence. The documented ability to synthesize, combine and prioritize supports this inference, but not a more specific architecture. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

### Retrieval at inference time

**DOCUMENTED**

- Saved memories operate similarly to custom instructions and form part of the context used to generate a response; legacy saved memories are “always considered” until deleted. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- With chat-history reference, relevant information from prior conversations may be introduced into new chats. ChatGPT does not retrieve every detail. ([Saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work))
- Newer UI can show sources used for personalization—custom instructions, chats, files and memories—and explain why a memory was used, although OpenAI warns the source display may not show every factor. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- Within non-enterprise projects, ChatGPT prioritizes project chats and files when answering; project-only memory imposes a hard source boundary. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))

**NOT DOCUMENTED**

OpenAI does not disclose whether retrieval uses embeddings, keyword search, recency scoring, memory importance scores, a separate retrieval model or a fixed token budget. Claims about those mechanisms should be labeled inference, not product fact.

### User control, deletion and Temporary Chat

**DOCUMENTED**

- Users can ask “What do you remember about me?”, explicitly correct/forget information, edit the memory summary, delete individual/all memories, or disable memory. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- Deleted saved memories may remain in safety/debug logs for up to 30 days. Removing a memory does not rewrite mentions already present in old chat transcripts. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- Disabling memory is not necessarily deletion: old saved memories remain unless separately removed. If memory is re-enabled while old source chats remain, ChatGPT may learn from those chats again. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- **Temporary Chat** does not access or create personalization memories, does not appear in history and is not used for model training; OpenAI may retain a copy for up to 30 days. Custom instructions still apply. Limited prior context may still be used in rare safety/security cases, so Temporary Chat is not an absolute “no contextual processing” guarantee. ([Temporary Chat FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-faq))

### Projects and boundaries

**DOCUMENTED**

- At project creation, users choose **default** or **project-only** memory; existing default projects cannot simply be converted—users must create a new project. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))
- Project-only memory does not reference account saved memories, allows retrieval from chats inside that project, and blocks chats outside it. Shared projects become permanently project-only and cannot access members’ personal context, custom instructions or outside memories. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))
- Default behavior differs by plan: Enterprise/Edu project chats remain contained; non-enterprise default projects can reference outside chats unless a project-only boundary prevents it. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))
- Project memory has no personal-memory-style list of individual project memories; it operates through the project’s conversations and resources. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))

### Enterprise/admin

Workspace controls can disable memory and other tools across projects; retention, residency, audit and access rules inherit workspace policy. Business/Enterprise/Edu project information is not used for model training by default. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt), [Enterprise privacy](https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/))

---

## 2. Anthropic Claude

### Consumer Claude memory

**DOCUMENTED**

- Anthropic launched Claude memory in September 2025 for Team/Enterprise and extended it to Pro/Max in October. It is explicitly optional and enabled from Settings. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- At initial setup, Claude generates memory from existing chats. The retained representation presented to users is a single **memory summary**, not a ChatGPT-style list of atomic saved-memory cards. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- The summary is directly visible; users update it conversationally and can tell Claude what to focus on or ignore. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- Each project gets a separate memory, intended to isolate different clients, confidential work and concurrent initiatives. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **Incognito chat** starts with a clean slate, does not appear in conversation history and does not read or write memory; ordinary memory/history remains unchanged. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- Enterprise admins can disable memory for the organization. Team/Enterprise standard retention settings continue to apply. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))

**INFERRED**

- Because Anthropic exposes one generated summary and says Claude adjusts it based on focus/ignore instructions, consumer Claude likely performs periodic or event-driven summarization rather than maintaining only independent fact records. Anthropic has not documented update frequency, confidence scoring, conflict precedence or whether additional hidden memory exists beyond the visible summary. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))

### Memory tool: separate developer primitive

The **Claude Platform memory tool must not be presented as the implementation contract for claude.ai memory**.

**DOCUMENTED**

- It is a client-side tool through which Claude requests persistent file operations. The host application—not Anthropic—stores and serves memory. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool))
- Claude automatically checks `/memories` before a task and may create/read/update/delete files during work. Retrieval is just-in-time, avoiding loading all memory into the context window. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool))
- Developers control namespace, storage, expiry and security. Anthropic recommends coherent/up-to-date files, deleting obsolete material, constraining what gets written, size caps and strict path traversal protection. ([Memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool))

### Difference from ChatGPT

- **Claude:** project separation is the organizing principle and the visible representation is a project-specific summary. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **ChatGPT:** historically exposes durable atomic saved facts plus a more fluid chat-history layer; project-only memory is optional rather than inherent to every project. ([Saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work), [Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))
- **Claude gives stronger visible summary editing; ChatGPT gives stronger atomic-memory deletion in its legacy mode.** Newer ChatGPT memory is converging toward Claude’s synthesized-summary model. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory), [OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

## 3. Google Gemini personal context

### Data sources and granularity

**DOCUMENTED**

1. **Saved info:** explicit durable details such as dietary restrictions, interests or a partner’s name. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/), [personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en))
2. **Past chats:** Gemini can derive relevant context from previous Gemini conversations. This first appeared for Advanced users and was announced for broader rollout. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
3. **Search history:** the 2025 Personalization experiment connects Gemini to raw Google Search activity, rather than merely storing a chatbot-generated profile. Google planned/introduced broader Google-app context such as Photos and YouTube. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))

### Retrieval and controls

- Users select the Personalization model/mode and explicitly approve the Search-history connection. Web & App Activity must also be on. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- Gemini analyzes each prompt and consults Search history only when its reasoning model determines history would improve the answer. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- The response can identify whether saved info, past chats or Search history was used. Users can disconnect Search history and view/manage the underlying Search activity. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- Google’s support documentation centralizes controls under personal context/personalization; availability varies by age, language, location, model and account type, especially work/school accounts. ([Personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en))

### Staleness/conflicts

**DOCUMENTED:** users can change/remove saved info and manage/delete underlying activity. Google documents conditional relevance at retrieval. ([Personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en), [Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))

**NOT DOCUMENTED:** Google does not explain how a contradiction between saved info, a recent chat and Search history is resolved, whether recency wins, or whether Search-derived preferences are persisted separately. Treat any such claim as inference.

### Privacy posture

Search personalization is affirmative-consent, source-transparent and revocable, making it the clearest opt-in among the four systems. However, it potentially exposes a much broader and more behaviorally sensitive raw dataset than fact/summarization memory. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/), [Privacy Hub](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en))

## 4. Microsoft Copilot memory and personalization

### Product model

**DOCUMENTED**

Microsoft announced in April 2025 that consumer Copilot would remember facts about users and use them to tailor future interactions, recommendations and proactive assistance. Users could tell Copilot to remember information and ask what it knew. ([Microsoft announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/))

**THIRD-PARTY REPORTED**

- Launch reporting described automatic accumulation of interests/preferences alongside explicit “remember” requests, plus user deletion and opt-out controls. ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/643225/microsoft-copilot-ai-features-memory-actions-vision), [GeekWire](https://www.geekwire.com/2025/microsoft-gives-copilot-its-own-memory-in-new-push-to-personalize-its-ai-assistant/))
- Microsoft later exposed a more directly editable profile under personalization/memory settings, according to hands-on reporting. ([ZDNET](https://www.zdnet.com/article/you-can-now-edit-microsoft-copilots-memories-about-you-heres-how/))

### Documented gaps

Microsoft’s public consumer material is less precise than OpenAI’s, Anthropic’s or Google’s documentation. It does **not** clearly specify:

- whether stored memory is atomic facts, a synthesized summary or both;
- extraction criteria and confidence thresholds;
- conflict/staleness precedence;
- inference-time retrieval mechanics;
- a project-scoped boundary comparable to Claude Projects or ChatGPT project-only memory;
- a dedicated incognito conversation mode with a documented no-read/no-write memory guarantee.

These should not be filled in from UI behavior without labeling the result as third-party observation.

### Consumer versus enterprise

Consumer memory is tied to the personal Copilot companion. Microsoft 365 Copilot’s organizational context is a different mechanism: it grounds responses through Microsoft Graph and honors existing identities, permissions, retention, audit and compliance controls. Microsoft states customer prompts, responses and Graph-grounded data are not used to train foundation models. ([Microsoft 365 privacy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy))

### Conflict and staleness

- **ChatGPT is most explicit:** new memory was designed to update stale facts and reconcile contradictions automatically. Exact precedence remains undisclosed. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- **Claude:** user can edit the one canonical summary and instruct focus/ignore; no documented automatic conflict algorithm. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **Gemini:** retrieval is relevance-gated and underlying sources are manageable, but cross-source conflict precedence is undocumented. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- **Copilot:** editing/deletion exists, but conflict/staleness behavior is not adequately documented. ([ZDNET](https://www.zdnet.com/article/you-can-now-edit-microsoft-copilots-memories-about-you-heres-how/))

### Consent, privacy and deletion

- **Best explicit source consent:** Gemini asks before connecting Search history and shows the contributing source. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- **Best session-level escape hatches:** ChatGPT Temporary Chat and Claude Incognito both provide no personalization-memory read/write; ChatGPT documents a 30-day safety copy and limited safety-context exception. ([OpenAI Temporary Chat](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-faq), [Claude memory](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **Deletion is source-sensitive:** ChatGPT explicitly warns that deleting the abstraction is insufficient if the source chat/file remains; this is an important general property of derived memory systems. ([Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))
- **Training consent is separate from memory consent:** turning memory off does not inherently delete history, and model-training controls are separate. OpenAI and Microsoft separately document enterprise no-training defaults. ([OpenAI Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt), [Microsoft 365 privacy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy))

### Opt-out/default posture

- **Claude:** documented opt-in; user enables it in Settings. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **Gemini Search personalization:** documented opt-in; requires explicit connection and Web & App Activity. ([Google announcement](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))
- **ChatGPT:** controls are independently configurable, but rollout defaults have varied by plan, region and memory generation. The stable documented point is that users can enable saved memory only, saved memory plus chat history, or neither. ([Saved-memory reference](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11146739-how-does-reference-saved-memories-work))
- **Copilot:** optional and disableable, but first-party material does not consistently specify a universal rollout default; do not claim one. ([Microsoft announcement](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/04/04/copilot-your-ai-companion/), [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/643225/microsoft-copilot-ai-features-memory-actions-vision))

### Enterprise/admin controls

- **OpenAI:** workspace memory/tool controls, RBAC for projects/sharing, compliance API, inherited retention/residency/audit controls and project isolation. ([Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))
- **Anthropic:** Enterprise admin can disable consumer memory; retention policy continues to apply. ([Anthropic announcement](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
- **Google:** personal-context feature availability is restricted for some work/school accounts; Google Workspace data governance should not be assumed equivalent to the consumer Search-history experiment. ([Personalization help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15637730?hl=en))
- **Microsoft:** Microsoft 365 Copilot relies on tenant identity, Graph permissions and Purview/compliance controls; that is organizational grounding, not the consumer memory feature. ([Microsoft 365 privacy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy))

## Design lessons for remembering a professor’s teaching and assessment preferences

1. **Use a typed, inspectable profile—not only raw-chat retrieval.** Store explicit fields such as course, level, assessment type, permitted resources, question-style mix, Bloom-level targets, grading strictness, notation, accommodations and formatting. Raw sessions should remain provenance, not the canonical preference record. This combines ChatGPT’s durable-fact approach with Claude’s editable summary. ([OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq), [Claude memory](https://claude.com/blog/memory))

2. **Separate professor-global from course/project-local memory.** Global: “prefers concise stems,” “uses partial credit,” “avoid trick questions.” Local: “CHEM-201 midterm is closed-book, 75 minutes, no spectroscopy.” Default to project/course isolation so one class cannot contaminate another, following Claude’s separate-project memory and ChatGPT project-only boundaries. ([Claude memory](https://claude.com/blog/memory), [ChatGPT Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt))

3. **Require confirmation for high-impact assessment rules.** Automatically infer low-risk style preferences, but make exam duration, learning outcomes, allowed materials, grading weights and accommodations explicit/confirmed memories. Consumer products permit implicit writes, but assessment errors have higher consequences. ([OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

4. **Attach provenance and timestamps to every memory.** Example: `prefers 40% application questions`, source `BIO-220 final planning, 2026-03-04`, confidence `explicit`. Surface “why this affected the exam,” analogous to OpenAI’s memory-source explanations and Gemini’s source transparency. ([OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq), [Google personalization](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-personalization/))

5. **Make conflict resolution visible.** Never silently merge “closed-book” and “open-note.” Show the conflict, favor the most recent explicit course-local statement over inferred/global memory, and ask for confirmation before generation. OpenAI’s stale-memory experience demonstrates why unattended contradictory facts degrade personalization. ([OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

6. **Provide a pre-generation memory checkpoint.** Before authoring an exam, display the exact profile slice to be applied: course scope, assessment constraints and style preferences. Let the professor edit it inline or proceed without memory.

7. **Offer a true no-memory session.** A “Private exam session” should neither read nor write professor memory, while making retention behavior explicit, following Temporary Chat/Incognito rather than a vague history toggle. ([OpenAI Temporary Chat](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-faq), [Claude memory](https://claude.com/blog/memory))

8. **Delete derived memory and its provenance together—or explain why not.** A professor deleting an assessment preference should be shown whether source transcripts remain capable of recreating it. OpenAI’s multi-source deletion requirement is the clearest warning against “delete card only” UX. ([OpenAI Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq))

9. **Retrieve just in time and within scope.** Load stable high-priority rules into every exam-authoring context; retrieve detailed examples/rubrics only when relevant. Anthropic’s developer memory tool explicitly documents this approach as a way to preserve context-window capacity. ([Claude memory tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool))

10. **Give institutional admins policy controls without taking authorship control from professors.** Admins should govern enablement, retention, residency, audit/export and sensitive-data categories; professors should control their profile and course boundaries. This mirrors OpenAI/Anthropic enterprise separation between workspace policy and personal/project memory. ([OpenAI Projects](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt), [Claude memory](https://claude.com/blog/memory))
